directAnswer: St. Marcellinus was the twenty-ninth bishop of Rome, from 296 until his death around 304, and he led the Church when Diocletian’s Great Persecution broke out in 303. Some ancient sources accused him of handing over Scriptures or offering incense under pressure, while others, including St. Augustine, denied the charge. He is venerated as a saint, and his feast has traditionally been kept on April 26.

paras: In February 303, Diocletian issued the first of several edicts ordering churches destroyed, Scriptures surrendered, and Christian meetings banned, followed by orders that clergy be imprisoned and forced to sacrifice. It was the most severe persecution the Church had faced. Marcellinus was bishop of Rome during these years.

The Liberian Catalogue gives the dates of his pontificate, but the Roman calendar of 354 does not include him among the martyrs or the bishops it commemorates, which has led historians to ask whether something about his conduct was disputed.

During the Donatist controversy in North Africa, some Donatists claimed that Marcellinus had handed over sacred books and offered incense to the gods. Augustine rejected this as an unproven slander. Later, the Liber Pontificalis repeated a version in which Marcellinus offered incense, then repented and was martyred, and a document describing a council at Sinuessa where he confessed his fault is now recognized as a forgery.

Historians remain divided about what happened. What is certain is that the Church honors him as a saint. He was buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria, and after his death the Roman Church went several years without a bishop.

keyFacts: Twenty-ninth bishop of Rome, June 30, 296, to c. October 25, 304
Led the Church at the start of Diocletian’s Great Persecution (303)
Accused by Donatist sources of lapsing; St. Augustine denied the charge
The story of a council at Sinuessa is a later forgery
Buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla; traditional feast day April 26

faqs.question: Did Pope Marcellinus offer sacrifice to pagan gods?
faqs.answer: Some Donatist writers claimed he handed over Scriptures and offered incense, and the Liber Pontificalis tells of a lapse followed by repentance. St. Augustine called the charge unproven, and the documents supporting the story are considered unreliable or forged. Historians have not reached a firm conclusion.

faqs.question: Why was there a gap after Pope Marcellinus died?
faqs.answer: The persecution under Diocletian and its aftermath made it impossible for the Roman Church to elect a successor for several years. Marcellus I was not chosen until 308.
